question: Team ES2013 weighed several energy sources for their remote. Which options were discussed, which one did they settle on in their third meeting, and was it still the choice in the final costing?
gold: Batteries (including the idea of a rechargeable internal battery), solar power and kinetic energy were discussed. In meeting c the consensus was kinetic energy, if at all possible, and in meeting d the final costing still used a single kinetic energy source.
answer: The team discussed standard (AA) batteries, a rechargeable internal battery, wind-up/hand dynamo, kinetic, and solar (solar was dropped as it fails in the dark and would be too heavy and costly). In the third meeting, Speaker A (Project Manager) summed up the consensus as using kinetic if at all possible, pending cost. In the fourth meeting's spreadsheet costing, kinetic was still the choice, with just one energy component needed.

citations.quote: So the consensus seems to be use the kinetic if it's at all possible.
Kinetic is um and how many of those will we need per we only need one.
which the choices that we've discussed were pretty much battery, kinetic or solar.

judge_note: Nothing material. Candidate covers batteries (including rechargeable internal), solar and kinetic, adds wind-up/dynamo as an extra option, gives kinetic as the consensus in the third meeting, and confirms kinetic with a single energy component in the final costing.

question: In Team IS1006, who first proposed making the remote out of titanium and why, what was said about rubber as an alternative, and which material did the final design keep?
gold: Speaker B proposed titanium in meeting b, for a baby-proof, unbreakable remote with a good style. In meeting c rubber was weighed (Speaker D liked its spongy feel; Speaker C said rubber is expensive and hard to shape), but in meeting d they stuck with titanium.
answer: Speaker B (User Interface Designer) first proposed titanium in IS1006b, arguing it would make the remote baby-proof, unbreakable and universal in style. In IS1006c, Speaker C (Industrial Designer) favoured titanium over rubber because rubber is expensive and harder to shape. The final design in IS1006d kept titanium.

citations.quote: I think that to make a baby-proof remote control it got to be a titanium. It's a really good style
We'll use mainly for titanium rubber is expensive and also it's bit difficult to do all the shapes
But we still didn't want to go far from our titanium idea

judge_note: The candidate leaves out Speaker D's remark in meeting c that rubber has a nice spongy feel, so its account of the rubber discussion is one-sided. It also says Speaker C 'favoured titanium over rubber', which the reference does not say; the reference only has C calling rubber expensive and hard to shape. 'Universal in style' is a loose match for 'good style'. The rest is correct: B proposed titanium in meeting b for a baby-proof, unbreakable remote, and the final design kept titanium.

question: What energy source did Team ES2015 choose, what happened to the idea of a solar backup, and what did the energy source cost in their final costing?
gold: They chose kinetic energy (Speaker B, the Industrial Designer, favoured it in meeting c). A solar backup was suggested in meeting c but dropped in favour of going fully kinetic. In meeting d the kinetic source was costed at three Euros, described as quite a large expense.
answer: The team chose a kinetic energy source. Speaker B (Industrial Designer) floated solar as a backup instead of a battery, but Speaker A (Project Manager) called it impractical, and the team later decided to go with kinetic alone and no backup. In the final costing, kinetic power cost three Euros.

citations.quote: Yeah. I think that might be a little impractical though.
Energy, we've decided on kinetic, right?
Okay we're using kinetic which is quite a large expense at three Euros.

judge_note: Nothing missing. The candidate matches the reference on kinetic energy, the solar backup being dropped for fully kinetic, and the three Euro cost. Its extra details (who suggested solar, the project manager calling it impractical, 'instead of a battery') are not in the reference, so I could not check them, and they do not contradict it.

question: Team IS1004 considered both an LCD screen and speech recognition. Which was ruled out first, in which meeting was the other ruled out, and what arguments were made against the LCD?
gold: Speech recognition was ruled out first, in meeting b, while the LCD was left open. The LCD was dropped in meeting c, because of cost against the 25 Euro price target and because Speaker D (Marketing Expert) argued it needed an internet connection and more requirements.
answer: Speech recognition was ruled out first: in IS1004b Speaker A (Project Manager) said the team would not go for it, while the LCD stayed open. The LCD was ruled out later, in IS1004c, where the team confirmed there would be no LCD. Speaker D (Marketing Expert) argued against it because it needs an internet connection and more components, so buying it is more than just buying a remote. Speaker A had also said earlier that the target price could not cover both an LCD and speech recognition.

citations.quote: we don't go for speech recognition technology.
I'm not convinced about this L_C_D_ because you need uh internet connection, you need more things
Okay right. Good. So no L_C_D_.

judge_note: Nothing material. Candidate matches: speech recognition ruled out first in meeting b, LCD ruled out in meeting c, with Speaker D's arguments about internet connection and more requirements. Cost argument is mentioned (target price can't cover both), though the 25 Euro figure is not stated; this is a minor omission.

question: What power source did Team IS1004's industrial designer propose, and what happened to the solar cells in the final meeting and why?
gold: Speaker C (Industrial Designer) proposed rechargeable batteries with a base (docking) station plus solar cells. In meeting d Speaker B (User Interface Designer) argued solar cells were no longer necessary with a recharging base station, and the team decided against them.
answer: Speaker C (Industrial Designer) proposed two power sources: ordinary batteries (rechargeable via a base station) plus solar cells for good lighting. In the final meeting the team dropped the solar cells and stuck with one rechargeable battery, because the rechargeable batteries with a base station made solar cells unnecessary and would also bring the cost down.

citations.quote: we can have two kind of power supplies, one is the usual batteries which are there, they could be chargeable batteries if there's a basis station kind of thing
I don't really know if the solar cells are actually necessary any more if you have a recharging base station.
I think rechargeable batteries will take care of the power thing. Yeah. To bring the cost

judge_note: Core facts match: Industrial Designer proposed rechargeable batteries with a base station plus solar cells, and the solar cells were dropped in the final meeting because the base station made them unnecessary. However, the candidate does not attribute the argument to the User Interface Designer (Speaker B), and adds unsupported details (lower cost, 'one rechargeable battery', 'good lighting'). Describing the proposal as 'two power sources' is also loosely worded.

question: Did Team ES2005 keep speech recognition in their final design, and what happened to the screen idea and why?
gold: Yes: speech recognition was voted in during meeting b and the final design in meeting d is mainly speech-operated, with buttons on the flip side. The LCD screen was dropped: in meeting c Speaker D argued it was too expensive for the 12.50 Euro budget and not right for an easy-to-use product, so the final design has no screen.
answer: Yes, they kept speech recognition: in ES2005b Speaker C (Project Manager) had the team vote and settled on speech recognition with limited buttons and organic design, and it carried through to the final prototype that relies mainly on speech recognition. The TFT screen idea was dropped after a vote in which no one supported it, with cost and fragility as concerns: Speaker A (Industrial Designer) said speech recognition is much cheaper than the TFT and that a TFT screen could easily break.

citations.quote: Who wants T_F_T_? No-one does. Excellent, so we'll go with speech recognition, yeah?
there's a good chance the the T_F_T_ screen would break or uh get damaged. They're pretty fragile.
Oh no it's it's much cheaper than the T_F_T_, it's just a microphone and some some integrated circuits.

judge_note: Speech recognition kept is correct (voted in b, final design mainly speech-operated), though the buttons on the flip side are not mentioned. The screen part differs from the reference: the reference says the LCD screen was dropped in meeting c because Speaker D argued it was too expensive for the 12.50 Euro budget and not right for an easy-to-use product. The candidate places the drop after a vote, attributes it to Speaker A, and cites fragility and cost relative to speech recognition. It omits meeting c, Speaker D, the 12.50 Euro budget, and the easy-to-use argument, and it adds claims the reference does not support.

question: What production cost limit was Team IS1000 working to, what did their more advanced design with speech recognition cost in the final meeting, and how much of that was the speech recognition?
gold: The limit was 12.50 Euros per unit (stated in meeting a and repeated in meeting d as non-negotiable). The advanced design came to 16 Euros, out of budget, of which the speech recognition system was about 3 Euros (about 13 without it); the basic version was about 8 Euros.
answer: Team IS1000 was working to a production cost limit of twelve euros fifty cents (12.50 euros). In the final meeting, Speaker C (User Interface Designer) said the more advanced design with speech recognition cost sixteen euros, of which about three euros was the speech recognition, leaving thirteen euros without it. The team ultimately cut speech recognition and went with the basic design at about twelve euros.

citations.quote: we will we can make this for for twelve Euro fi and fifty cents.
they say basically that the S_R_ system would be uh something like three Francs per item so three Euros sorry.
So that takes it down to thirteen Euros without the speech recognition.

judge_note: Nothing missing on the key facts: limit 12.50 euros, advanced design 16 euros, speech recognition about 3 euros (13 without). The extra claims that the team cut speech recognition and went with a basic design at about 12 euros are not contradicted by the reference, which gives the basic version as about 8 euros. That detail is a small discrepancy, but it is not what the question asked.

question: What power source and case did Team IS1001 agree on in their third meeting, and were these kept in the final meeting?
gold: In meeting c they agreed on a standard battery and an odd (banana) shape with a spongy cover. Meeting d kept both: a standard battery and a yellow banana-shaped case with a rubber material around it.
answer: In the third meeting, the team agreed on a standard battery and a spongy, banana-shaped case (Speaker A, Project Manager, confirmed the spongy case). Both were kept in the final meeting: Speaker A (Project Manager) reviewed the costing with a standard battery and a yellow banana-shaped case with rubber material around it to feel spongy.

citations.quote: So we will just use a a standard battery?
I think it's the box that should be spongy, banana's shape.
to have a standard battery, to have a yellow banana shaped uh case with uh a rubber material around it

judge_note: Nothing material. The candidate matches the reference: standard battery and spongy banana-shaped case in meeting 3, both kept in the final meeting (yellow banana shape with rubber material). The speaker attribution is extra detail and does not contradict the reference.

question: Team TS3012 had agreed to put both an LCD screen and speech recognition in their remote. What happened to these in their final meeting, and what reason was given?
gold: Changed finances forced a cut in meeting d: Speaker A (Project Manager) proposed taking out speech recognition and keeping the LCD, because about ninety percent of users favoured an LCD display but only sixty percent favoured speech recognition.
answer: In the final meeting, speech recognition was dropped from the base product. Speaker C (Industrial Designer) said it cannot be done at this price, so customers who want it must pay more. The LCD screen was kept because Speaker A (Project Manager) judged it worth more than speech recognition and said it would be the one to keep if something had to go for affordability.

citations.quote: But if pep people really want speech recognition, then they must be prepared to pu to pay more, because it's cannot be done for this.
I think the L_C_D_ screen is more worth than speech recognition.

judge_note: Core outcome matches: speech recognition dropped, LCD kept. But the stated reason differs. The reference gives user-preference figures (about 90% favoured LCD vs 60% favoured speech recognition), and the changed finances forcing the cut. The candidate instead cites Industrial Designer saying speech recognition can't be done at this price and the Project Manager judging the LCD worth more. The user-preference percentages are missing, and the candidate attributes part of the reasoning to a different speaker.

question: When Team TS3008 reviewed energy sources, which option was preferred, and did the push for kinetic power in their final meeting change the design?
gold: Speaker C preferred a basic battery when presenting the options in meeting c. In meeting d Speaker A pushed for a kinetic part as a special feature, but it did not make it in: the design stayed with one battery, and A said they would have liked a kinetic part as well.
answer: The preferred energy source was the basic battery: Speaker C (Industrial Designer) favoured it over kinetic or solar, and kinetic and solar were seen as odd for a remote. In the final meeting Speaker A (Project Manager) pushed for kinetic power, but Speakers C and D objected. A ended by saying they would have liked a kinetic part and then "we leave it like this", so the push did not change the design. The memory ledger's 'kinetic-only' decision conflicts with this closing exchange, so I relied on the transcript.

citations.quote: the basic battery, which I thi prefer because of its uh its non uh non-depending of of of uh um
I would li I would have liked a kinetic part as well, to give it some just to give it some extra special feature
Okay, well we leave it like this.

judge_note: Nothing material. The candidate matches the reference: C preferred the basic battery, A pushed for kinetic in the final meeting, and the design did not change. Extra details (C and D objecting, the memory ledger conflict) don't contradict the reference.

question: Did voice recognition make it into Team ES2012's final remote, and what voice features did the final design have?
gold: Yes. Voice recognition, pushed by Speaker A from meeting b and confirmed in meeting c, is in the final design in meeting d: a microphone for voice commands, plus a spoken 'where are you' function to find the remote.
answer: Yes, voice recognition made it into the final design. In ES2012d Speaker A (Project Manager) said the voice sensor was expensive but a fundamental decision that had to stay, and Speaker B (Industrial Designer) presented the prototype with a microphone for voice commands. Voice came alongside physical controls (a volume scroll, channel up/down buttons, a large power key and a menu key), not as a buttonless voice-only remote.

Uh we got a microphone there which for all the voice commands so you can you know talk to it like that and it'll still understand.
And we've been talking about it the whole time. Anyway, I'm I'm incli kinda inclined to say that we should just go for it.

judge_note: Candidate confirms voice recognition is in the final design with a microphone for voice commands, but omits the spoken 'where are you' function for finding the remote. It also doesn't mention that Speaker A pushed it in meeting b and it was confirmed in meeting c.
